#3242. 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Security leaders reveal the future consequences of AI outpacing human defenders.

At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

The capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the new reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s new security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

According to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of new software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, says cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain

Bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a new, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security issues, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security issues introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against new and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance

CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

#3241. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:

#3240. Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Apple is leaning into AI-powered health tools with the launch of its Apple Health AI Usage Study.

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for

Participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now

The AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google launched its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” said Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this new health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

#3239. Why Micron Stock Crashed Today

TrendForce warns: NAND prices are suddenly falling.

By Rich Smith – Nov 20, 2026 at 11:34AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›

Micron (MU -13.17%) stock tumbled 10.6% through 11:20 a.m. ET Friday morning, and I know what you're thinking:

Anthropic IPO'd yesterday at $83 a share, opened at $111.50 -- a 34% gain -- and then closed at $97.17 -- a 13% loss for anyone who bought in at the open. It's not quite a broken IPO, but for many investors it probably feels like one, and it may be making investors in other artificial intelligence-related stocks nervous. It doesn't help that Anthropic is down another 10.4% today.

But I think there's another reason why Micron stock is down today.

As StreetInsider.com reports today, memory-market research firm TrendForce just published a negative forecast for NAND flash memory demand in 2027.

Major Chinese cloud providers are likely to cut orders for enterprise SSDs next year, TrendForce warns. Indeed, they're already cutting orders, and NAND spot prices are already down 20% "as distributors clear inventory." This decrease in demand may eliminate pricing pressure on NAND chips, forcing NAND prices lower in Q1 2027, in Q2 2027, and "onward."

Now, the good news for Micron is that it doesn't just sell NAND. Actually, only about 26% of the company's revenue comes from NAND, with the balance coming from sales of DRAM. This means that Micron won't be as sensitive to NAND price declines as Sandisk (SNDK -16.09%), for example.

Investors also have to be alert to the risk that the same dynamics that depress demand for NAND may also affect DRAM demand. If we see demand and prices decline there as well, then Micron may fail to dodge this bullet.

Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

“Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple said on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ plans, starting with the 27.3 release.”

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:

One positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ plan.

#3231. Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the company’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time …

Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.)

I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy users at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an update, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that currently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

#3230. Prediction: This Quantum Computing Stock Will Be the Biggest Winner of 2027

Pasqal is down more than 80% from its peak, but it could be 2027's big comeback story if its next machine shows up on time.

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 20, 2026 at 11:47AM EST

If you only looked at Pasqal Holding (PSQL +5.33%) stock's chart, you'd assume something broke. The French quantum computer maker hit $24.69 a share within days of its Nasdaq debut in late August. Today, it trades at around $3.

But when I dug into what the company has actually been doing, I didn't find a broken business. I found one that's ahead of its stock. That gap is why I think Pasqal could be the biggest winner in quantum computing next year.

There are numerous ways to create the quantum bits — aka, qubits — that sit at the heart of every quantum computer.

Pasqal is taking the “neutral-atom qubit” approach, creating each qubit from a single rubidium atom held in place and manipulated by lasers. One advantage of this method is that its machines don't need powerful cryogenic cooling systems to bring them to temperatures near absolute zero, which some more commonly pursued qubit technologies require.

That makes it easier to install them in the same rooms as ordinary server racks, and Pasqal has seven of them deployed across three continents, plus factories in France and Canada built to turn out up to 13 machines a year. CEO Wasiq Bokhari says that its hardware design will scale to at least 10,000 qubits per machine by 2029.

"Customers don't care whether it's a quantum computer or a GPU," he told analysts in June. "They just want the problem solved."

The best example among its current customers is energy megacap Saudi Aramco, which formally launched a 200-qubit Pasqal machine at its data center in May and now offers cloud access to it for other companies.

"Aramco is not just waiting for quantum computing, it is helping to shape it," Bokhari said. Pasqal has also signed a partnership with LG's tech arm in South Korea and a joint venture agreement to deploy systems across Saudi Arabia. It even launched a plug-in that lets AI coding assistants turn a research idea into a running experiment on its cloud machines.

The big catalyst due to arrive in 2027 is Vela, the next machine on Pasqal's roadmap, which will have 200-plus qubits. CTO Loïc Henriet described Vela as the machine that will "bring the first quantum advantage use cases to our clients." In plain English, that means it should be able to solve real business problems faster than a traditional GPU-powered server cluster can. Pasqal also aims to have systems providing 20 error-corrected "logical" qubits in production by 2027.

The science is already getting interesting. In October, its 256-qubit processor revealed magnet behavior that theory didn't predict. "We are not simply reproducing what we already know, but uncovering behavior we did not expect," Henriet said.

The catch is that roadmaps slip. Vela is a target, not a product on a shelf, and if it arrives late or underwhelms, the 2027 story will fall apart.

The business’s financial numbers are small and bumpy. In the third quarter, revenue fell to 3.3 million euros, from 5.7 million euros a year earlier, because Pasqal sold no machines during the quarter. Revenue from services like cloud access, upgrades, and maintenance did jump 53%, but that wasn't enough to compensate for the lack of new quantum computer orders. However, Bokhari said: "Although the order book and revenue do not show it yet, we have made important progress in our technology roadmap."

In September, Pasqal also exited a French defense quantum program to focus on commercial work. The cash story is mixed, too. In June, CFO Stéphane Rougeot said the SPAC merger that it was using to join the public market could leave Pasqal with "north of $600 million." In August, the actual deal netted it about $360 million. During its analyst day presentation in June, Rougeot also mentioned that the company had secured a $250 million convertible note, which could turn into new shares and dilute today's owners.

Here's why I still like the setup. Pasqal ended September with 312.8 million euros in cash and equivalents on its balance sheet, and its market cap is only about $681 million. Rougeot said annual cash burn has been between 30 million euros and 50 million euros, should rise only modestly, and that "we have plenty of runway." At this price, investors are paying very little for the technology itself.

That's what makes a "biggest winner" call possible. A stock already priced for disappointment doesn't need perfection to soar. Pasqal just needs Vela to show up and work. If it delivers its first system providing a quantum advantage to customers in 2027, I expect the market will stop pricing it as a failed experiment.

#3227. Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You can make space on your console for GTA 6 a few different ways.

The wait is over. Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive. The game is 212 GB, which means it takes up about half of the storage space on my Xbox Series S. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game. Here’s what you should know about these options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 is available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to buy either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, you won’t get the highest visual quality and you will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

I chose the cheapest option and deleted a few games from my Xbox. I’m not planning on leaving GTA 6 any time soon.

#3224. Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”

#3223. Black Friday Sales Are Days Away, but Most US Adults Aren’t Waiting, CNET Finds

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over one-third have already started holiday shopping, but November's sales could yield big savings.

Even though early holiday sales started months ago, shopping your wish lists during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales may be worth the wait if you’re one of the few planning to shop November sales. It’s the time to save money on most tech devices. But holiday shopping could look different for US adults juggling smaller budgets and shopping frustrations.

CNET’s annual holiday shopping survey shows that 27% of US adults plan to start holiday shopping in November and 17% plan to shop during sales. However, US adults will be juggling a smaller tech budget of $808. That’s $123 less than CNET’s survey findings last year.

Finding savings is paramount to staying within your price range this year, but how can you spot a good deal when nearly every retailer is having a sale? CNET experts weighed in on US adults’ holiday shopping plans and shared expert advice to score the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals on must-haves.

CNET found that 27% will plan or start their holiday shopping this month, with 17% of November shoppers planning to shop holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The big question is whether the sales are worthwhile. CNET’s director of commerce content, Russell Holly, says it comes down to when you find a deal on a must-have item.

“The best time to buy is the moment you see something you want on an actual discount, because increased prices can come at any time,” Holly said.

Holly says even steep discounts aren’t lowering prices as much as before, but the right deals may make you reconsider. You just have to know where and when to shop for tech devices.

For example, Black Friday is usually the best time to buy electronics, including TVs and robot vacuums, with the biggest deals lasting from Black Friday to Cyber Monday.

CNET’s senior laptops editor, Matt Elliott, says if you’re planning to buy a new laptop during holiday sales, look for discounts at Amazon, Best Buy and vendor sites like Dell, HP and Lenovo.

“These retailers and companies are constantly rotating discounts on laptops, and these sales can save you hundreds of dollars. So, it’s worth tracking the price of a laptop you want and buying it when it dips,” said Elliott.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday are also a good time to buy the latest wearables, said CNET’s wearable expert, Vanessa Hand Orellana.

“For Black Friday, all the heavy wearable hitters tend to go on sale: Google, Samsung, Oura, Garmin and Apple,” said Orellana. However, if you don’t need the latest tech, you can find some of the best deals on last year’s tech at third-party retailers, like Best Buy and Walmart. And many of the previous-gen models share the same features as the newest ones, said Orellana.

CNET’s deals team spends hours making sure sales are legitimate — not just a fake price drop. And in the coming weeks, they’ll track deals on devices like laptops, headphones, wearable devices and smart home gadgets, plus alternatives to more costly tech, to help you determine what’s worth buying now or later.

You can also check an item’s price history to see if you’re getting the best deal by using price trackers like CamelCamelCamel and comparing prices across retailers before buying. But as Holly noted, if you want to upgrade your personal devices, don’t wait. Look for the best price you can find and buy it right away. Otherwise, prices may go up while you wait.

Last year, CNET found that US adults planned to spend an average of $931 on holiday shopping. This year, shoppers are planning to spend less.

On average, they expect to spend $808 on holiday shopping. That’s $123 less than last year. Some generations plan to spend more, such as millennials, who anticipate an average holiday shopping outlay of $1,074. Boomers will spend around half that amount — $582.

Higher everyday living costs could explain why holiday budgets are lower.“Everything else being more expensive means less left over for gifts,” said Holly. “There’s very little indication that component prices are going to come back down anytime soon, so if you’re hoping for the kinds of prices you saw even two years ago, I would say you’re going to be waiting quite a while.”

Balancing holiday gifts and everyday basics on your usual income can be a lot to handle. Now’s the time to set holiday expectations, including a budget and a list of must-haves, along with more affordable options that still meet your needs.

Then keep checking prices and deals from your trusted retailers and be prepared to buy when you spot good savings. Most importantly, try to avoid using credit cards and buy-now, pay-later plans that can lead to debt. The Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike held rates elevated, which means borrowing costs will remain high and make debt more expensive through higher credit card and loan interest rates.

CNET found that 73% of shoppers plan to buy tech products or services this season, but what most US adults plan to buy and how much they plan to spend may surprise you.

Thirty percent of shoppers plan to purchase toys, and 25% plan to buy kitchen items, such as air fryers and cookware. But shoppers don’t plan to buy as many personal electronics and home entertainment products. Only 20% plan to buy headphones or earbuds, and even fewer plan to buy video games for consoles (18%) or laptops and TVs (11%). More shocking is that only 13% plan to buy phones. We’ve seen prices increase across popular tech devices and brands due to the RAM shortage, which has led to low supply and high demand for memory chips.

Some of the latest releases cost way more than the average $808 most US adults plan to spend. For instance, the $2,000 iPhone Duo alone costs even more than the average $1,704 that millennials plan to spend on tech this holiday season. And less costly phones are still beyond holiday budgets, like the $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro Max, and even the iPhone 18 Pro is $1,200. Trade-in offers and sales can help lower that cost if you’re planning to upgrade, but shop around and compare deals before buying.

Increased prices may make you reconsider whether to stick with your current model or upgrade, but remember, you have options.

“If the current laptop works well enough, upgrading can either be viewed as a luxury purchase for later or shifted to buying used or refurbished models to save extra,” Holly said.

You may also consider a slightly older model of the device you’re looking for. It could still have all of the features you need, but cost less. Another money-saving option is to consider refurbished tech that’s in excellent or good condition from a certified refurbished retailer. You may still notice some price increases due to demand, but it could still cost less than the newest models.

Most US shoppers (84%) expect the holiday shopping season to come with a few hurdles this year. Forty-three percent are concerned about deceptive pricing practices, such as retailers raising original prices before discounting them for a sale. Others are concerned about deals selling out immediately because of low stock or automated buying bots (39%).

But if you’re more worried about fake deals or sales being a money grab by retailers, Holly said that historically, there have been some great sales ahead of the holidays. It’s still best to do your research before buying to make sure you’re getting a deal by comparing retailer prices before and after announced sales and using price tracking tools, like CamelCamelCamel. Heads up that many retailers, like Amazon, have flash sales with specific times of deeper discounts, and you’ll need to act fast, so it’s best to plan your holiday shopping now.

“The best thing anyone can do ahead of a shopping event is prepare,” said Holly. “Find your favorite price tracker tool before the event starts, have a general idea of what you’re looking to buy and be sure to keep an eye out for bigger discounts when you bundle things together.”

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,615 adults, of whom 1,552 were interested in purchasing consumer tech products or services this winter holiday season. Fieldwork was undertaken Sept. 3-6, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 and older).

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

This auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.)

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast

Outside of these new features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the update, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

Starring Anthony Boyle as FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried and three-time Emmy winner Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison—the CEO of FTX's sister hedge fund Alameda Research and Sam's on-and-off-again girlfriend—the eight-part limited series follows the couple's transformation from ambitious young idealists trying to revolutionize the finance world to culprits in an $8 billion scheme that upended the entire crypto market.

The stacked ensemble cast includes Alex Lawther, Karan Soni, Matt Rife, Madison Hu, Paul Reiser, Jennifer Grey, Robin Weigert and "Heated Rivalry" star Hudson Williams.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

If you don't know him for his cooking, then you do for his cool: The late, great Anthony Bourdain was one of the most singular figures to come out of the culinary world, so it's no surprise that he'd be the subject of a high-profile bio-drama.

But instead of charting Bourdain's days as a hotshot chef in top New York kitchens, this Matt Johnson-directed biopic takes it back to the toque's beginnings as an impulsive 19-year-old (played by "The Holdovers" standout Dominic Sessa) working a summer dishwasher job at a local restaurant in 1970s Provincetown, Massachusetts. Under the tutelage of Chef José Vatel (Antonio Banderas) and the gritty restaurant crew, Tony B. gets his first real taste of the chaos and triumphs of a professional kitchen.

The A24 flick—which also stars Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Stavros Halkias, and real-life chef icon Eric Ripert—will make its subscription streaming debut on HBO Max on Saturday, November 20.

The final chapter of "Yellowjackets" is finally here, with the survival drama's fourth season premiering on Paramount+ on Friday, November 20. But if you, like yours truly, are a bit behind on the psychological thriller, a long Sunday catching up with the unhinged antics of Shauna (played by Sophie Nélisse in the past and Melanie Lynskey in the present), Taissa (Jasmin Savoy Brown and Tawny Cypress), Misty (Samantha Hanratty and Christina Ricci) and the rest of the gang sounds like a day well spent.

If you're not familiar, "Yellowjackets" follows a 1996 high school girls' soccer team in the aftermath of a plane crash, which leaves them stranded deep in the remote Canadian wilderness. Their fight for survival descends into a psychological nightmare as the girls begin dabbling in ritualized cannibalism, group hunts, and other cultish mysticism. In a parallel timeline set in the present day, the adult survivors must reckon with those dark secrets and long-held regrets 25 years later.

#3216. Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills – and share them

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Google is retiring Gemini Gems. Here's what to do to access the same tools as Skills.

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that says “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.)

A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google says. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

Next, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

While these new models might be useful for AI power users, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the company rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

#3213. Chewy vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Chewy's recurring pet revenue goes head-to-head with MercadoLibre's Latin American fintech and commerce empire, and the valuation gap may tip the scales.

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 12:00PM EST

Does the stability of the pet category outweigh the high growth of Latin American e-commerce? Choosing between Chewy Inc. (CHWY -2.48%) and MercadoLibre Inc. (MELI +0.57%) requires balancing recurring revenue against regional market dominance.

Chewy focuses on the North American pet market through specialized fulfillment and a high-margin subscription model. MercadoLibre operates a massive integrated commerce and fintech ecosystem across 18 countries in Latin America. Investors often compare them to see if a niche leader or a geographic titan offers better long-term potential.

Chewy operates as a leading online retailer for pet owners, providing everything from food and toys to prescription medications. The company partners with approximately 4,000 brands and has developed its own private labels such as Frisco and American Journey. A significant portion of its business comes from the PracticeHub platform, which is currently used by roughly 50% of all veterinary clinics in the United States. This specialized focus among retail stocks allows the company to build deep loyalty through subscription-like programs.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached about $13.1 billion. This represented growth of roughly 5.9% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for the period was about $273.7 million, as the company continues to focus on improving profitability through its high-margin Autoship subscription service and pharmacy sales.

As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, meaning total debt is equal to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, is roughly 0.9x. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow was around $562.4 million. Note that for the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since stock-based compensation is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

MercadoLibre provides an integrated commerce and financial services ecosystem across 18 different countries in Latin America. Its Marketplace platform facilitates both direct sales and third-party transactions, supported by an extensive logistics network known as Mercado Envios. The company also operates Mercado Pago, a fintech powerhouse that handles online payments, credit, and asset management for millions of users. By combining these services, the company captures growth from both the rise of digital shopping and the increasing adoption of digital financial tools in emerging markets.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $38.5 billion. This reflected significant growth of approximately 47.1% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for those 12 months was around $1.9 billion, showcasing the company's ability to generate significant profits while expanding its footprint across the region.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.7x, indicating that total debt is 1.7 times the value of shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is approximately 1.2x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was about $10.8 billion, representing the cash remaining after the business pays for its operations and capital expenses.

Chewy faces intense competition from mass merchants and large online retailers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -3.71%) that can use their scale to lower prices. The business relies heavily on third-party shipping and the performance of its own fulfillment centers to maintain customer satisfaction. Regulatory changes in pet pharmacy and telehealth, along with the risk of cybersecurity incidents compromising customer data, could also impact future operations.

MercadoLibre operates in several volatile economies, making it susceptible to high inflation and currency fluctuations in markets like Brazil and Argentina. It faces competition from both global e-commerce players and local financial institutions entering the fintech space. Extensive regional regulations covering banking and data protection, combined with the logistical challenges of operating across 18 countries, present ongoing risks for the business.

Chewy appears to be the more value-oriented choice based on its lower Forward P/E, which measures price against future earnings estimates, and its lower P/S ratio, which compares market value to sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

MercadoLibre is in another year of heavy investment, as the company continues to expand its Mercado Envios and Mercado Pago platforms. The business delivered another strong quarter in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026. Net revenue surpassed $10 billion for the second straight quarter, growing 46% year-on-year after 50% growth in the second quarter. Net income was $488 million, which was modest growth that fell below analysts' expectations. There is some margin compression going on, however, due to higher energy costs resulting from the Iran war.

For the full year 2026, analyst consensus is that MercadoLibre will see revenue around $41 billion, a big $11 billion jump from 2025. That should come with net income of $1.8 billion, a figure that analysts have been revising downward largely due to energy price pressure.

Chewy is establishing a steady growth pattern. In a recently reported quarter, management noted that its Autoship program grew faster than overall sales, implying that many customers' standing orders will continue to provide a solid base for the company. The company also believes that in the long run, veterinarian and general pet health services are a huge untapped market for Chewy. The business recently closed on the acquisition of Modern Animal, which delivers high profitability per location and is a strong complement to Chewy's existing business.

For fiscal 2027, sales are seen rising 7% to $13.5 billion, with net income up more than 40% to around $317 million, according to consensus analyst estimates. American consumers have shown they will spend more to take care of their pets.

However, Chewy likely doesn't have a great competitive moat against brick-and-mortar competitors like PetSmart and Petco Health and Wellness Co.(WOOF -2.22%).

So which stock is the better addition to your 2027 portfolio? MercadoLibre comes at a premium valuation that may not be justified by Latin American consumer spending. This view is falling back on historical behavior, given the U.S. consumer has traditionally been the more reliable spender in good times and bad. Since Chewy comes at a cheaper valuation relative to MercadoLibre, it's the stock to buy.

#3212. Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft announced two new AI models at Ignite 2026 that promise impressive performance for much lower cost. They could reshape its relationship with OpenAI and Anthropic for good.

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two new frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first

A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

There’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

#3211. iOS 27 has clever new Messages feature I’ve been using a lot

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

The idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the new version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

That’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

The only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

#3209. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.
